findings.title: @phildavson7552
findings.snippet:
I was a roadie for small locals bands working the Sydney music scene in 1981-2. The Sets, the Allnighters, the Mansel rooms at Kings Cross was our local hangout that had great bands where we ended up at after the gigs. Lots of places in Darlinghurst, Surrey Hills, saw the Triffids live which was great. Most of the time i was off my face and i cant remember much except we supported the lime spiders a few times. Then there was Sydney Uni and supporting Inxs there. The Angels were massive, the Divynls, The Hitman and the Bel Aires. Saw the Clash and all hell broke out with mods and Stray Cats in support. Complete mayhem. 
Loved the scene, i wish i could remember more venues.
Cheers Phil

findings.title: @manonymous4737
findings.snippet:
I was around at that exact time too! The weekly ritual was to grab OTS and see who was playing, it was a seemingly endless round of Painters and Dockers, Bored!, You Am I when they were still good, Hard-Ons, Warped, Died Pretty, Nunbait, Cosmic Psychos, Psychotic Turnbuckles, New Christs, Beasts of Bourbon (SO many times!) and Rifles Rifles Rifles! Deniz Tek played a surprisingly large number of times, too, I'd never miss one of his gigs. One time Dark Carnival came on tour at the same time as Tek, that was a big week, 4 nights of Ronnie Asheton and 3 for Tek! It didn't matter if I went on my own, I was guaranteed to run into many people I knew as it was the same great venues, Annandale,  Phoenecian, Lansdowne, Hopetoun, what was that one halfway down the hill from the Hopetoun? Heading down towards the Evil Star..... I videotaped a Hard-ons gig there on a huge VHS film camera.
Now all I have is memories, and your channel of course

findings.title: @delmontemansaysyes
findings.snippet: Thanks Gioia, love your work! That's a pretty comprehensive summary of the demise of Sydney's live music culture. It's impossible to blame any one factor but it seems true that all these things happened to combine over a period of time to bring this golden era to a close. Same things I guess that conspired to create it in the first place but in reverse! One thing for certain though is we will never see the likes of this period again so we need to cherish our memories of the bands, venues and people that built and sustained it for about 15 years. Feels like something of a live music revival is taking place right now in Sydney and even though it won't return to the halcyon days we need to get out there and pay our money to keep it alive or else we will be condemned to sitting at home watching the 7.30 report forever!!

findings.title: @markgrovenor389
findings.snippet: Thanks for sharing your thoughts! I played live from 1985 when I left high school until late 90's but so many things conspired to deter live music. I always blamed pokies taking over the band rooms but as you say, drink driving, residential development with associated noise regulations and even GST impacted on bands getting paid, which was previously cash in hand and beers! I am just glad i got to enjoy some of the glory years!
